'Hi Chris, while checking the Dashboard test cases against the spec (version 44) and the Claude design, we found a few points only you can decide. Please write your answer in the yellow column; a letter such as (a) or (b) is enough.

'When a tile's trend line is flat (for example Technician Utilization at 100% on every day), where should it sit?
(a) Along the bottom of the small trend area, as the build draws it today.
(b) At its real level, so 100% does not look like 0%.
(c) Should we add your answer to the spec, so the tests can follow it?

'Ayesha asked this in Slack on 9 Oct and you answered that the line "should read as a flat". The spec does not say where a flat line sits, and the squad's working rules say a decision only counts once it is in the spec.
'Release note for the Sales and Service Advisor Analysis reports

'The published release note says totals can drop. When an invoice is voided and then invoiced again for more, the figures can go up.
(a) Should the note also say that a figure can go up in that case?
(b) Or is the note complete as published?
'The developers' tech plan (16 Sep) asked the note to mention this case. Your published note (10 Oct) does not.

'The spec lists nine date choices for a tile (This Month, Last Month, and so on). The build also offers "Today" and a calendar to pick any range.
(a) Should a tile offer "Today"?
(b) Should a tile offer a custom range from the calendar?
'Recent bug reports and one of Vladimir's test cases use "Today" and the calendar on the tiles. The spec and the release notes list the nine choices only.

'In the expanded At Risk Customers table, should a customer's 12-month revenue be a link that opens the Sales report filtered to that customer?
(a) Yes, it should be a link.
(b) No, it is plain text.
'One test case expects a link. We found no sentence about it in the spec, the stories, the release notes, the comments or Slack.

'When you open the details of the Revenue tile, should the chart always show one bar per month for the last twelve months, whatever date range the tile is set to?
(a) Yes, always twelve monthly bars.
(b) No, it should follow the tile's date range.
'A bug report expected monthly bars and was fixed on 9 Oct. The spec describes the small trend line on the tile, but not the bars in the expanded chart.

'In the expanded Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization charts, what should a month with no value look like?
(a) A gap in the line.
(b) A dashed line joining the months either side, as the design shows.
'The spec says how the small trend line on a tile handles an empty period (a gap), and that the expanded charts are "unchanged". It does not say what an empty month looks like in an expanded chart.
'Report link on the technician tiles with no data

'The approved drawing for tiles with no data shows no report link (the small arrow) on the Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization tiles. The spec says every tile keeps its report link and the empty state "changes nothing else on the tile".
(a) Keep the report link on those two tiles (the spec).
(b) Remove it when the tile has no data (the drawing).
'Revenue, Billing Efficiency and Sales by Customer keep their arrow in the same drawing.

'The design's note says the At Risk card measures revenue "the way Sales By Customer does". The spec says it is measured "the way the Revenue tile measures revenue" (subtotals before discount and tax, minus credit memos).
(a) Like the Revenue tile (the spec).
(b) Like Sales by Customer (the design note).
'The two ways can give different figures for the same customer, so the At Risk tests depend on the answer.
'At Risk with no customers at risk

(a) "$0.00 (12mo) · 0 customers", as the design shows.
(b) Something else (please write it).
(c) No line at all.
'The spec covers one customer and more than one customer, but not zero.

'The design shows two places to choose the inactivity period: the pill on the tile and an "Inactive for" box inside the expanded panel. The spec mentions one control.

(b) Both, always showing the same value.
